sentences.text: Hardness crept up to 240 ppm overnight — someone check whether the crushed coral bag split. Dim lights keep the wild bettas calm, so we work by headlamp when netting out pairs. Nobody warned me that angelfish eat their first three clutches before figuring out parenthood. I mark each spawning jar's lid with tape: date, pair number, hardness at laying. Eggs stuck to the heater cord again, which means scraping and praying half survive the move. He logs GH and KH in a spiral notebook, one column per shelf, dated in pencil. Every runt gets fed to the bichir; sentiment doesn't pay for fish food. Her ledger shows which pairings threw long fins and which threw nothing worth keeping. Honestly, half our overtime comes from grinding out sloppy tack welds the day shift leaves behind. Third rejection this week on bay two's seams—somebody check that wire feed. Her ultrasonic probe traced the seam twice; the second pass found the void the first had missed. Sparks rained off the hull plate while two welders argued, through their visors, about last night's match. Under the floodlights, the half-finished chassis looked less like a war machine and more like a beached steel whale. The shift supervisor taped the rejection slip to the chassis and told nobody to touch it until the metallurgist arrived. All armored side panels shall be degreased, inspected for lamination defects, and logged before entering the assembly line. Nine bare chassis sat in line for turret installation, but only one crane operator was scheduled before noon. Quality inspectors rejected fourteen hull plates on Tuesday after ultrasonic testing revealed porosity along the lower weld seams. A hairline crack in the mantlet casting sent the whole batch back to the foundry, three weeks of schedule gone. Watch the sling angle, Marek—if that turret assembly swings into the jig again, we lose the whole morning. Crane four to floor: lowering the turret in thirty seconds, clear the ring. What is the meaning of the word tank?
